sentences.zh: 王懿 張邵

translations.literal: Wang Yi, Zhang Shao
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi and Zhang Shao

sentences.zh: 趙倫之，字幼成，下邳僮人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Lunzhi, style name Youcheng, was a man of Tong in Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lunzhi, styled Youcheng, was a native of Tong in Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 孝穆皇后之弟。

translations.literal: He was the younger brother of Empress Xiaomu.
translations.idiomatic: He was the younger brother of Empress Xiaomu.

sentences.zh: 幼孤貧，事母以孝稱。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor in youth, he was known for serving his mother with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor from childhood, he was known for serving his mother with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 武帝起兵，以軍功封閬中縣五等侯，累遷雍州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu raised his army, he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Langzhong County for military merit, and was promoted repeatedly to Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu raised his army, Lunzhi was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Langzhong County for military merit and was promoted repeatedly to Inspector of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 武帝北伐，倫之遣順陽太守傅弘之、扶風太守沈田子出嶢柳，大破姚泓於藍田。

translations.literal: During Emperor Wu's northern campaign, Lunzhi sent Shunyang Administrator Fu Hongzhi and Fufeng Administrator Shen Tianzi out through Yao Willow, and they routed Yao Hong at Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Wu's northern campaign, Lunzhi sent Shunyang Administrator Fu Hongzhi and Fufeng Administrator Shen Tianzi out through Yao Willow Pass and they routed Yao Hong at Lantian.

sentences.zh: 及武帝受命，以佐命功，封霄城縣侯，安北將軍，鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the Mandate, for his role in founding the dynasty he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiaocheng County, made General Who Pacifies the North, and stationed at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu received the Mandate, Lunzhi was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiaocheng County for his founding service, appointed General Who Pacifies the North, and stationed at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，徵拜護軍。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor ascended the throne, he was summoned and appointed Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor ascended the throne, Lunzhi was summoned and appointed Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年，拜鎮軍將軍，尋遷左光祿大夫，領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia, he was appointed General Who Guards the Army; soon after he was transferred to Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and made General Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanjia he was appointed General Who Guards the Army; soon after he was transferred to Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and made General Who Leads the Army.

sentences.zh: 倫之雖外戚貴盛，而以儉素自處。

translations.literal: Although Lunzhi was an exalted imperial in-law, he maintained an austere and simple manner.
translations.idiomatic: Although Lunzhi was an exalted imperial in-law, he lived in frugal simplicity.

sentences.zh: 性野拙，人情世務，多所不解。

translations.literal: By nature he was rough and unrefined, and understood little of human affairs and worldly business.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was rough and unrefined, and understood little of human relations or worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 久居方伯，頗覺富盛，入為護軍，資力不稱，以為見貶。

translations.literal: Having long served as a regional governor, he had grown accustomed to wealth and splendor; when he entered the capital as Protector of the Army, his abilities did not match the post, and he felt he had been demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Having long served as a regional governor, he had grown accustomed to wealth and grandeur; when he entered the capital as Protector of the Army, his talents no longer matched his station, and he took this as a demotion.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫范泰好戲謂曰：「司徒公缺，必用汝老奴。

translations.literal: Grand Master for Splendid Happiness Fan Tai, jesting, said to him: "The Minister over the Masses is vacant — they are sure to use you, old fellow.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master for Splendid Happiness Fan Tai, joking, said to him: "The post of Minister over the Masses is vacant — they are sure to use you, old fellow.

sentences.zh: 我不言汝資地所任，要是外戚高秩次第所至耳。

translations.literal: I am not speaking of your talents and the post you deserve — it is simply the usual progression for illustrious in-laws to high rank, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: I am not speaking of your talents and the post you deserve — it is simply the usual progression for exalted in-laws to high rank, that is all."

sentences.zh: 」倫之大喜，每載酒肴詣泰。

translations.literal: " Lunzhi was greatly pleased and each time brought wine and food when visiting Fan Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Lunzhi was greatly pleased and each time brought wine and delicacies when visiting Fan Tai.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanjia he died.

sentences.zh: 子伯符嗣。

translations.literal: His son Bofu succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bofu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 伯符，字潤遠。

translations.literal: Bofu, style name Runyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bofu, styled Runyuan.

sentences.zh: 少好弓馬。

translations.literal: In youth he loved archery and horsemanship.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 倫之在襄陽，伯符為竟陵太守。

translations.literal: While Lunzhi was at Xiangyang, Bofu served as Administrator of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: While Lunzhi was stationed at Xiangyang, Bofu served as Administrator of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 時竟陵蠻屢為寇，伯符征討，悉破之，由是有將帥之稱。

translations.literal: At the time the Man tribes of Jingling raided repeatedly; Bofu campaigned against them and crushed them all, and thereby gained a reputation as a commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Man of Jingling raided repeatedly; Bofu campaigned against them and defeated them all, and thereby gained a reputation as a commander.

sentences.zh: 後為寧遠將軍，總領義徒，以居宮城北，每有火起及賊盜，輒身貫甲胄，助郡縣赴討，武帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Later he was made General of Distant Peace, commanded loyal followers, and lived north of the palace; whenever fires broke out or bandits appeared, he would arm himself in armor and help the commanderies and counties in pursuit, and Emperor Wu greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made General of Distant Peace and commanded loyal followers, living north of the palace; whenever fire broke out or bandits appeared, he would don armor himself and help the commanderies and counties in pursuit, and Emperor Wu greatly praised him.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，累遷徐、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he was promoted repeatedly to Inspector of Xu and Yan Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, Bofu was promoted repeatedly to Inspector of Xu and Yan Provinces.

sentences.zh: 為政苛暴，吏人畏之若豺虎，然而寇盜遠竄，無敢犯境。

translations.literal: His governance was harsh and cruel; officials and people feared him like wolves and tigers, yet bandits fled far away and none dared violate his borders.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was harsh and cruel; officials and people feared him like wolves and tigers, yet bandits fled far away and none dared violate his borders.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十八年，徵為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Yuanjia, he was summoned to serve as General Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Yuanjia he was summoned to serve as General Who Leads the Army.

sentences.zh: 先是，外監不隸領軍，宜相統攝者，自有別詔，至此始統領焉。

translations.literal: Previously, the Outer Command did not come under the General Who Leads the Army; whoever was to command them received a separate edict — only at this point did he begin to command them as a body.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Outer Command did not fall under the General Who Leads the Army; whoever was to supervise them received a separate edict — only at this point did he begin to command them as a whole.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，轉豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, he was transferred to Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to Inspector of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 明年，為護軍將軍，復為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: The next year he became Protector of the Army and again served as Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became Protector of the Army and again served as Governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 在郡嚴酷，吏人苦之，或至委叛被錄赴水而死；

translations.literal: In the commandery his rule was severe and cruel; officials and people suffered under it, and some even deserted after being arrested and drowned themselves in the water;
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery his rule was severe and cruel; officials and people suffered bitterly, and some were driven so far that they deserted, were arrested, and drowned themselves in the river;

sentences.zh: 典筆吏取筆不如意，鞭五十。

translations.literal: a clerk in charge of writing implements took up a brush that did not please him, and he had him flogged fifty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: a clerk in charge of writing brushes selected one that did not please him, and Bofu had him flogged fifty strokes.

sentences.zh: 子倩，尚文帝第四女海鹽公主。

translations.literal: His son Qian married Emperor Wen's fourth daughter, the Princess of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qian married Emperor Wen's fourth daughter, the Princess of Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 初，始興王濬以潘妃之寵，故得出入後宮，遂與公主私通。

translations.literal: At first Prince of Shixing Liu Jun, through the favor of Consort Pan, was allowed free entry to the inner palace, and thereupon had a secret affair with the princess.
translations.idiomatic: At first Prince of Shixing Liu Jun, through the favor of Consort Pan, was allowed free entry to the inner palace, and thereupon carried on a secret affair with the princess.

sentences.zh: 及適倩，倩入宮而怒，肆詈搏擊，引絕帳帶。

translations.literal: When she was married to Qian, Qian entered the palace in a rage, cursed and struck freely, and tore apart the curtain ties.
translations.idiomatic: When she was married to Qian, Qian entered the palace in a rage, cursed and struck wildly, and tore apart the bed-curtain ties.

sentences.zh: 事上聞，有詔離婚，殺主所生蔣美人，伯符慚懼發病卒。

translations.literal: The matter reached the throne; an edict ordered divorce and put to death Lady Jiang, the princess's birth mother; Bofu, ashamed and afraid, fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: The matter reached the throne; an edict ordered divorce and put to death Lady Jiang, the princess's birth mother. Bofu, ashamed and afraid, fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 諡曰肅。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Su.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Su.

sentences.zh: 傳國至孫勖，齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: The fief passed to his grandson Xu; when Qi received the abdication, the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The fief passed to his grandson Xu; when Qi received the abdication, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 王懿，字仲德，太原祁人。

translations.literal: Wang Yi, style name Zhongde, was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi, styled Zhongde, was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 自言漢司徒允弟幽州刺史懋七世孫也。

translations.literal: He claimed to be the seventh-generation descendant of Mao, younger brother of Han Minister over the Masses Wang Yun and Governor of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed to be the seventh-generation descendant of Mao, younger brother of Han's Minister over the Masses Wang Yun and Governor of You Province.

sentences.zh: 祖宏，事石季龍；

translations.literal: His grandfather Hong served Shi Jilong;
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hong served Shi Jilong;

sentences.zh: 父苗，事苻堅，皆為二千石。

translations.literal: his father Miao served Fu Jian; both held posts of the two-thousand-bushel rank.
translations.idiomatic: his father Miao served Fu Jian; both held posts of the two-thousand-bushel rank.

sentences.zh: 仲德少沈審，有意略，通陰陽，解聲律。

translations.literal: Zhongde from youth was deep and careful in judgment, possessed strategic ability, understood yin and yang, and could interpret pitch and mode.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zhongde was deep and careful in judgment, possessed strategic ability, understood yin and yang, and could interpret pitch and mode.

sentences.zh: 苻氏之敗，仲德年十七，與兄睿同起義兵，與慕容垂戰，敗；

translations.literal: When the Fu clan fell, Zhongde was seventeen; he and his elder brother Rui together raised a righteous army and fought Murong Chui — and were defeated;
translations.idiomatic: When the Fu clan fell, Zhongde was seventeen; he and his elder brother Rui together raised a righteous army and fought Murong Chui — and were defeated;

sentences.zh: 仲德被重創走，與家屬相失。

translations.literal: Zhongde, seriously wounded, fled and lost contact with his family.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde, seriously wounded, fled and lost contact with his family.

sentences.zh: 路經大澤，不能前，困臥林中。

translations.literal: Passing through a great marsh, he could not go forward and, exhausted, lay down in the forest.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through a great marsh, he could not go forward and, exhausted, lay down in the forest.

sentences.zh: 忽有青衣童兒騎牛行，見仲德，問曰：「食未？

translations.literal: Suddenly a boy in green robes riding an ox came along; seeing Zhongde, he asked: "Have you eaten yet?
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a boy in green robes riding an ox came along; seeing Zhongde, he asked: "Have you eaten yet?

sentences.zh: 」仲德告饑。

translations.literal: " Zhongde told him he was starving.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde told him he was starving.

sentences.zh: 兒去，頃之復來，攜食與之。

translations.literal: The boy left; before long he returned, carrying food and giving it to him.
translations.idiomatic: The boy left; before long he returned, carrying food and giving it to him.

sentences.zh: 仲德食畢欲行，會水潦暴至，莫知所如。

translations.literal: When Zhongde had finished eating and wished to go on, sudden flooding arrived and he knew not where to go.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongde had finished eating and wished to go on, sudden flooding arrived and he knew not where to go.

sentences.zh: 有一白狼至前，仰天而號，號訖，銜仲德衣，因渡水；

translations.literal: A white wolf came before him, lifted its head and howled to heaven; when it had finished howling, it took Zhongde's garment in its mouth and thus crossed the water;
translations.idiomatic: A white wolf came before him, lifted its head and howled to heaven; when it had finished howling, it took Zhongde's garment in its mouth and thus crossed the water;

sentences.zh: 仲德隨之，獲濟，與睿相及。

translations.literal: Zhongde followed it, succeeded in crossing, and rejoined Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde followed it, succeeded in crossing, and rejoined Rui.

sentences.zh: 渡河至滑臺，復為翟遼所留，使為將帥。

translations.literal: Crossing the river to Huatai, he was again detained by Zhai Liao and made a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the river to Huatai, he was again detained by Zhai Liao and made a commander.

sentences.zh: 積年，仲德欲南歸，乃奔太山，遼遣騎追之急，夜行，忽有炬火前導，仲德隨之，行百許里，乃免。

translations.literal: After years, Zhongde wished to return south, so he fled to Mount Tai; Liao sent cavalry in hot pursuit; traveling by night, suddenly torches led the way before him — Zhongde followed them for about a hundred li and thus escaped.
translations.idiomatic: After years, Zhongde wished to return south, so he fled to Mount Tai; Liao sent cavalry in hot pursuit. Traveling by night, suddenly torches led the way before him — Zhongde followed them for about a hundred li and thus escaped.

sentences.zh: 晉太元末，徙居彭城。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jin Taixuan era, he moved his residence to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jin Taixuan era, he moved his residence to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 兄弟名犯晉宣、元二帝諱，並以字稱。

translations.literal: The brothers' personal names tabooed the posthumous names of Jin's Emperors Xuan and Yuan, so all were known by their style names.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers' personal names tabooed the posthumous names of Jin's Emperors Xuan and Yuan, so all were known by their style names.

sentences.zh: 睿字元德。

translations.literal: Rui's style name was Yuande.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's style name was Yuande.

sentences.zh: 北土重同姓，謂之骨肉，有遠來相投者，莫不竭力營贍；

translations.literal: In the north kinsmen prized shared surnames and called one another "flesh and bone"; when distant kin came seeking refuge, none failed to exert themselves to provide for them;
translations.idiomatic: In the north kinsmen prized shared surnames and called one another "flesh and bone"; when distant kin came seeking refuge, none failed to exert themselves to provide for them;

sentences.zh: 若不至者，以為不義，不為鄉里所容。

translations.literal: those who did not receive them were deemed unrighteous and could not be tolerated in their community.
translations.idiomatic: those who did not receive them were deemed unrighteous and could not be tolerated in their community.

sentences.zh: 仲德聞王愉在江南，是太原人，乃往依之；

translations.literal: Zhongde heard that Wang Yu was in the Jiangnan region and was a man of Taiyuan, so he went to rely on him;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde heard that Wang Yu was in the Jiangnan region and was a man of Taiyuan, so he went to rely on him;

sentences.zh: 愉禮之甚薄，因至姑孰投桓玄。

translations.literal: Yu treated him very poorly, so he went to Gushu and attached himself to Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu treated him very poorly, so he went to Gushu and attached himself to Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 值玄篡，見輔國將軍張暢，言及世事，仲德曰：「自古革命，誠非一族，然今之起者，恐不足以成大事。」

translations.literal: When Xuan usurped the throne, he met General Who Assists the State Zhang Chang and spoke of current affairs; Zhongde said: "Revolutions from ancient times have indeed not been the work of one clan alone, yet those who rise up now, I fear, are not enough to achieve a great enterprise."
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan usurped the throne, he met General Who Assists the State Zhang Chang and spoke of current affairs. Zhongde said: "Revolutions from ancient times have indeed not been the work of one clan alone, yet those who rise up now, I fear, are not enough to achieve a great enterprise."

sentences.zh: 元德果敢有智略，武帝甚知之，告以義舉，使於都下襲玄。

translations.literal: Yuande was bold, resolute, and possessed of strategy; Emperor Wu knew him well, told him of the righteous rising, and sent him to strike at Xuan in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yuande was bold, resolute, and possessed of strategy; Emperor Wu knew him well, told him of the righteous rising, and sent him to strike at Xuan in the capital.

sentences.zh: 仲德聞其謀，謂元德曰：「天下之事，不可不密，應機務速，不在巧遲。

translations.literal: Zhongde heard of the plan and said to Yuande: "Affairs of the realm cannot but be kept secret; one must seize the moment with speed — success does not lie in clever delay.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde heard of the plan and said to Yuande: "Affairs of the realm cannot but be kept secret; one must seize the moment with speed — success does not lie in clever delay.

sentences.zh: 玄每冒夜出入，今若圖之，正須一夫力耳。

translations.literal: Xuan every night goes out at dusk; if one means to take him now, it would take only the strength of a single man.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan goes out every night at dusk; if one means to take him now, it would take only the strength of a single man.

sentences.zh: 」事泄，元德為玄所誅，仲德奔竄。

translations.literal: " The plot leaked; Yuande was executed by Xuan, and Zhongde fled in flight.
translations.idiomatic: The plot leaked; Yuande was executed by Xuan, and Zhongde fled.

sentences.zh: 會義軍克建業，仲德抱元德子方回出候武帝，帝於馬上抱方回，與仲德相對號泣，追贈元德給事中，封安復縣侯，以仲德為中兵參軍。

translations.literal: When the righteous army captured Jianye, Zhongde carried Yuande's son Fanghui out to meet Emperor Wu; the emperor, mounted on his horse, held Fanghui and wept face to face with Zhongde; Yuande was posthumously granted Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Marquis of Anfu County, and Zhongde was made Army Aide of the Centre.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army captured Jianye, Zhongde carried Yuande's son Fanghui out to meet Emperor Wu. The emperor, mounted on his horse, held Fanghui and wept face to face with Zhongde; Yuande was posthumously granted Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Marquis of Anfu County, and Zhongde was made Army Aide of the Centre.

sentences.zh: 武帝伐廣固，仲德為前鋒，大小二十餘戰，每戰輒克。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu attacked Guanggu, Zhongde served as vanguard; in more than twenty engagements large and small, he prevailed in every battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu attacked Guanggu, Zhongde served as vanguard; in more than twenty engagements large and small, he prevailed in every battle.

sentences.zh: 及盧循寇逼，敗劉毅於桑落，帝北伐始還，士卒創痍，堪戰者可數千人。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun's bandits pressed close, having defeated Liu Yi at Sangluo, the emperor had just returned from his northern campaign; the troops were wounded and weary, and those fit to fight numbered only a few thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun's bandits pressed close, having defeated Liu Yi at Sangluo, the emperor had just returned from his northern campaign; the troops were wounded and weary, and those fit to fight numbered only a few thousand.

sentences.zh: 賊眾十萬，舳艫百里，奔敗而歸者，咸稱其雄。

translations.literal: The rebels numbered a hundred thousand, their ships stretched for a hundred li, and those who had fled in defeat upon returning all proclaimed their might.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels numbered a hundred thousand, their ships stretched for a hundred li, and those who had fled in defeat upon returning all proclaimed their might.

sentences.zh: 眾議並欲遷都，仲德正色曰：「今天子當陽而治，明公命世作輔，新建大功，威震六合。

translations.literal: All in council wished to move the capital; Zhongde, with stern countenance, said: "Today the Son of Heaven governs from the yang position; my lord was born for this age to serve as chief minister, has newly built great merit, and his prestige shakes the six directions.
translations.idiomatic: All in council wished to move the capital. Zhongde, with stern countenance, said: "Today the Son of Heaven governs from the yang position; my lord was born for this age to serve as chief minister, has newly built great merit, and his prestige shakes the six directions.

sentences.zh: 妖賊豕突，乘我遠征，既聞凱入，將自奔散。

translations.literal: These demonic bandits rush like swine; taking advantage of our distant campaign, once they hear of our triumphant return they will scatter of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: These demonic bandits rush like swine; taking advantage of our distant campaign, once they hear of our triumphant return they will scatter of themselves.

sentences.zh: 今自投草間，則同之匹夫；

translations.literal: If we now cast ourselves into the grasslands, we become no different from common men;
translations.idiomatic: If we now cast ourselves into the grasslands, we become no different from common men;

sentences.zh: 匹夫號令，何以威物？

translations.literal: and what thing would obey the commands of a common man?
translations.idiomatic: and what thing would obey the commands of a common man?

sentences.zh: 義士英豪，當自求其主爾。

translations.literal: Men of righteousness and heroic spirit will seek out their own lord in any case.
translations.idiomatic: Men of righteousness and heroic spirit will seek out their own lord in any case.

sentences.zh: 此謀若行，請自此辭矣。

translations.literal: If this plan is pursued, I must take my leave from here.
translations.idiomatic: If this plan is pursued, I must take my leave from here.

sentences.zh: 」帝悅之，以仲德屯越城。

translations.literal: " The emperor was pleased and stationed Zhongde at Yuecheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and stationed Zhongde at Yuecheng.

sentences.zh: 及賊自蔡洲南走，遣仲德追之。

translations.literal: When the bandits fled south from Caizhou, he sent Zhongde in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits fled south from Caizhou, he sent Zhongde in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 賊留親黨范崇民五千人，高艦百餘，城南陵。

translations.literal: The rebels left five thousand of their kin and partisans under Fan Chongmin, with more than a hundred tall ships, south of Nanling.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels left five thousand of their kin and partisans under Fan Chongmin, with more than a hundred tall ships, south of Nanling.

sentences.zh: 仲德攻之，大破崇民，焚其舟艦，收其散卒，功冠諸將，封新淦縣侯。

translations.literal: Zhongde attacked them, routed Fan Chongmin, burned their ships, gathered their scattered troops; his merit surpassed all the generals, and he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingan County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde attacked them, routed Fan Chongmin, burned their ships, and gathered their scattered troops; his merit surpassed all the generals, and he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingan County.

sentences.zh: 義熙十二年北伐，進仲德征虜將軍，加冀州刺史，為前鋒諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yixi, during the northern campaign, Zhongde was promoted to General Who Conquers the Barbarians, given additional appointment as Inspector of Ji Province, and made Director of Campaign Affairs for the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yixi, during the northern campaign, Zhongde was promoted to General Who Conquers the Barbarians, given additional appointment as Inspector of Ji Province, and made Director of Campaign Affairs for the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍檀道濟、龍驤將軍王鎮惡向洛陽，寧朔將軍劉遵考、建武將軍沈林子出石門，寧朔將軍朱超石、胡藩向半城，咸受統於仲德。

translations.literal: Champion General Tan Daoji and Flying Dragon General Wang Zhen'e moved toward Luoyang; Pacifying the North General Liu Zunkao and General Who Establishes Martial Might Shen Linzi went out through Shimen; Pacifying the North General Zhu Chaoshi and Hu Fan moved toward Bancheng — all were under Zhongde's overall command.
translations.idiomatic: Champion General Tan Daoji and Flying Dragon General Wang Zhen'e moved toward Luoyang; Pacifying the North General Liu Zunkao and General Who Establishes Martial Might Shen Linzi went out through Shimen; Pacifying the North General Zhu Chaoshi and Hu Fan moved toward Bancheng — all were under Zhongde's overall command.

sentences.zh: 仲德率龍驤將軍朱牧、寧遠將軍竺靈秀、嚴綱等開鉅野入河，乃總眾軍，進據潼關。

translations.literal: Zhongde led Flying Dragon General Zhu Mu, General of Distant Peace Zhu Lingxiu, Yan Gang, and others to open the route from Juye into the river, then commanded all the armies and advanced to occupy Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde led Flying Dragon General Zhu Mu, General of Distant Peace Zhu Lingxiu, Yan Gang, and others to open the route from Juye into the river, then commanded all the armies and advanced to occupy Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 長安平，以仲德為太尉諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Chang'an was pacified, Zhongde was made Consulting Aide to the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang'an was pacified, Zhongde was made Consulting Aide to the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 武帝欲遷都洛陽，眾議咸以為宜。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu wished to move the capital to Luoyang; all in council deemed it fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu wished to move the capital to Luoyang; all in council deemed it fitting.

sentences.zh: 仲德曰：「非常之事，常人所駭。

translations.literal: Zhongde said: "An extraordinary undertaking alarms ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde said: "An extraordinary undertaking alarms ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 今暴師日久，士有歸心，固當以建業為王基，俟文軌大同，然後議之可也。

translations.literal: Our armies have been exposed in the field a long time; the soldiers yearn for home. We should surely take Jiankang as the royal foundation, wait until civilization and the imperial road are unified, and only then discuss it."
translations.idiomatic: Our armies have been exposed in the field a long time; the soldiers yearn for home. We should surely take Jiankang as the royal foundation, wait until civilization and the imperial road are unified, and only then discuss it."

sentences.zh: 」帝深納之，使衛送姚泓先還彭城。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply accepted this and had Yao Hong escorted back to Pengcheng first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply accepted this and had Yao Hong escorted back to Pengcheng first.

sentences.zh: 武帝受命，累遷徐州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the Mandate, Zhongde was promoted repeatedly to Inspector of Xu Province with additional designation as Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu received the Mandate, Zhongde was promoted repeatedly to Inspector of Xu Province with additional designation as Supervisor.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年，進號安北將軍，與到彥之北伐，大破虜軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia, his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North; with Dao Yanzhi he undertook a northern campaign and greatly routed the barbarian army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanjia his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North; with Dao Yanzhi he undertook a northern campaign and greatly routed the barbarian army.

sentences.zh: 諸軍進屯靈昌津。

translations.literal: The armies advanced and encamped at Lingchang Ford.
translations.idiomatic: The armies advanced and encamped at Lingchang Ford.

sentences.zh: 司、兗既定，三軍咸喜，仲德獨有憂色，曰：「胡虜雖仁義不足，而凶狡有餘，今斂戈北歸，并力完聚，若河冰冬合，豈不能為三軍之憂！

translations.literal: With Si and Yan provinces settled, all three armies rejoiced; Zhongde alone wore a look of concern and said: "The Hu barbarians, though lacking in benevolence and righteousness, have more than enough cunning and ferocity. Now they sheathe their blades and return north to gather their strength together — if the river freezes in winter and the ice joins, would that not become a worry for all three armies!
translations.idiomatic: With Si and Yan provinces settled, all three armies rejoiced; Zhongde alone wore a look of concern and said: "The Hu barbarians, though lacking in benevolence and righteousness, have more than enough cunning and ferocity. Now they sheathe their blades and return north to gather their strength together — if the river freezes in winter and the ice joins, would that not become a worry for all three armies!

sentences.zh: 」十月，虜於委粟津渡河，進逼金墉，虎牢、洛陽諸軍相繼奔走。

translations.literal: " In the tenth month the barbarians crossed the river at Weisu Ford and pressed toward Jinyong; the armies at Hulao and Luoyang fled one after another.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the barbarians crossed the river at Weisu Ford and pressed toward Jinyong; the armies at Hulao and Luoyang fled one after another.

sentences.zh: 彥之聞二城不守，欲焚舟步走，仲德曰：「洛陽既陷，則虎牢不能獨全，勢使然也。

translations.literal: Yanzhi, hearing that the two cities could not be held, wished to burn the ships and flee on foot; Zhongde said: "With Luoyang already fallen, Hulao cannot stand alone — such is the force of circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi, hearing that the two cities could not be held, wished to burn the ships and flee on foot. Zhongde said: "With Luoyang already fallen, Hulao cannot stand alone — such is the force of circumstances.

sentences.zh: 今賊去我千里，滑臺猶有強兵，若便舍舟奔走，士卒必散。

translations.literal: The enemy is now a thousand li from us, and Huatai still has strong troops; if we abandon the ships and flee at once, the soldiers will surely scatter.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is now a thousand li from us, and Huatai still has strong troops; if we abandon the ships and flee at once, the soldiers will surely scatter.

sentences.zh: 且當入濟至馬耳谷口，更詳所宜。

translations.literal: For now we should enter the Ji and reach the mouth of Ma'er Valley, and then consider more carefully what is fit.
translations.idiomatic: For now we should enter the Ji and reach the mouth of Ma'er Valley, and then consider more carefully what is fit.

sentences.zh: 」乃回軍沿濟南歷城步上，焚舟棄甲，還至彭城。

translations.literal: " They thereupon turned the army, marched by land along the Ji through Licheng, burned the ships and cast off their armor, and returned to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: They thereupon turned the army, marched by land along the Ji through Licheng, burned the ships and cast off their armor, and returned to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 仲德與彥之並免官。

translations.literal: Zhongde and Yanzhi were both stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde and Yanzhi were both stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 尋與檀道濟救滑臺，糧盡而歸。

translations.literal: Before long, with Tan Daoji he went to relieve Huatai; when provisions were exhausted they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, with Tan Daoji he went to relieve Huatai; when provisions were exhausted they returned.

sentences.zh: 九年，又為鎮北將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he again became General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yuanjia he again became General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 明年，加領兗州刺史。

translations.literal: The next year, he was additionally given concurrent appointment as Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was also given concurrent appointment as Inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 仲德三臨徐州，威德著於彭城，立佛寺作白狼、童子像於塔中，以河北所遇也。

translations.literal: Zhongde thrice took up post at Xuzhou; his authority and virtue were renowned at Pengcheng. He built a Buddhist temple and placed statues of the White Wolf and the Boy in its pagoda — in memory of what he had encountered north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Three times Zhongde held command at Xuzhou, and his authority and virtue were felt at Pengcheng. He raised a Buddhist temple and set images of the White Wolf and the Boy in its pagoda, commemorating what he had met with in the lands north of the River.

sentences.zh: 十三年，進號鎮北大將軍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, his title was advanced to General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year his title was advanced to General Who Guards the North.

sentences.zh: 十五年，卒，諡曰桓侯。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died; his posthumous title was Marquis Huan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he died and was posthumously titled Marquis Huan.

sentences.zh: 亦於廟立白狼、童子壇，每祭必祠之。

translations.literal: Altars to the White Wolf and the Boy were also erected in the temple, and at every sacrifice they were worshipped.
translations.idiomatic: Altars to the White Wolf and the Boy were also set up in the temple, and every sacrifice included offerings to them.

sentences.zh: 子正脩嗣，為家僮所殺。

translations.literal: His son Zhengxiu succeeded him and was killed by a household servant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhengxiu succeeded him but was killed by a household servant.

sentences.zh: 張邵，字茂宗，會稽太守裕之弟也。

translations.literal: Zhang Shao, styled Maozong, was the younger brother of Yu, Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shao, styled Maozong, was the younger brother of Yu, Administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 初為晉琅邪內史王誕龍驤府功曹，桓玄徙誕於廣州，親故咸離棄之，惟邵情意彌謹，流涕追送。

translations.literal: At first he served as Recorder in the Dragon-Charger office of Wang Dan, Interior Secretary of Langya under Jin. When Huan Xuan exiled Dan to Guangzhou, relatives and friends all abandoned him; only Shao grew ever more devoted in affection, weeping as he escorted him.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as Recorder in the Dragon-Charger office of Wang Dan, Interior Secretary of Langya under Jin. When Huan Xuan exiled Dan to Guangzhou, kin and friends alike deserted him; only Shao's devotion deepened, and he followed in tears to see him off.

sentences.zh: 時變亂饑饉，又饋送其妻子。

translations.literal: Amid the turmoil and famine of the times, he also sent provisions to Dan's wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: In those days of upheaval and famine, he also sent food and supplies to Dan's wife and children.

sentences.zh: 桓玄篡位，父敞先為尚書，以答事微謬，降為廷尉卿。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan usurped the throne, Shao's father Chang had previously served as Minister of the Masters of Writing; for minor errors in handling official correspondence he was demoted to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan usurped the throne, Shao's father Chang, who had previously served as Minister of the Masters of Writing, was demoted to Minister of Justice for slight errors in handling official business.

sentences.zh: 及武帝討玄，邵白敞表獻誠款，帝大說，命署其門曰：「有犯張廷尉者，以軍法論。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu campaigned against Xuan, Shao urged Chang to submit a memorial pledging loyalty. The Emperor was greatly pleased and ordered these words posted on his gate: "Whoever offends Minister of Justice Zhang shall be dealt with by military law.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu marched against Xuan, Shao persuaded Chang to submit a memorial pledging loyalty. The Emperor was greatly pleased and ordered these words posted on his gate: "Whoever offends Minister of Justice Zhang shall be dealt with by military law.

sentences.zh: 」後以敞為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: " Later Chang was appointed Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chang was appointed Administrator of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 王謐為揚州，召邵為主簿。

translations.literal: When Wang Mi served as Inspector of Yang Province, he summoned Shao as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mi served as Inspector of Yang Province, he summoned Shao to be his Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 劉毅為亞相，愛才好士，當世莫不輻湊，獨邵不往。

translations.literal: Liu Yi was Vice Prime Minister; he loved talent and honored scholars, and everyone in the age flocked to him — only Shao did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi served as Vice Prime Minister, loved talent, and honored scholars; everyone in the age flocked to him, yet Shao alone did not go.

sentences.zh: 或問之，邵曰：「主公命世人傑，何煩多問。

translations.literal: When someone asked why, Shao said: "Our lord is an outstanding man of the age — why trouble yourself with so many questions?
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why, Shao said: "Our lord is a towering figure of the age — why bother asking so much?

sentences.zh: 」劉穆之聞以白，帝益親之，轉太尉參軍，署長流賊曹。

translations.literal: " When Liu Muzhi heard this and reported it, the Emperor drew still closer to him, transferred him to staff officer under the Grand Commandant, and appointed him head of the Office for Bandits on the Long Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Muzhi heard this and reported it, the Emperor drew still closer to him, transferred him to staff officer under the Grand Commandant, and put him in charge of the Office for Bandits on the Long Rivers.

sentences.zh: 盧循寇迫京師，使邵守南城。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun's bandits pressed upon the capital, the Emperor sent Shao to hold the South Wall.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun's forces threatened the capital, the Emperor sent Shao to defend the South Wall.

sentences.zh: 時百姓臨水望賊，帝怪而問邵，邵曰：「若節鉞未反，奔散之不暇，亦何能觀望。

translations.literal: At the time the common people lined the waterside to watch the bandits. The Emperor found this strange and questioned Shao. Shao said: "If the imperial insignia had not yet returned, they would have been fleeing and scattering with no time to spare — how could they have stood watching?
translations.idiomatic: The common people were lining the waterside to watch the bandits. The Emperor found this strange and questioned Shao. Shao said: "If the imperial insignia had not yet returned, they would have been fleeing in every direction with no time to spare — how could they have stood watching?

sentences.zh: 今當無復恐耳。

translations.literal: Now they should have no fear left.
translations.idiomatic: Now they surely have nothing left to fear.

sentences.zh: 」尋補州主簿。

translations.literal: " Soon afterward he was supplemented as provincial Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed provincial Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 邵悉心政事，精力絕人。

translations.literal: Shao devoted himself wholeheartedly to administration; his energy surpassed all others.
translations.idiomatic: Shao gave himself wholly to administration, and his energy surpassed all others.

sentences.zh: 及誅劉藩，邵時在西州直廬，即夜誡眾曹曰：「大軍當大討，可各修舟船倉庫，及曉取辦。

translations.literal: When Liu Fan was executed, Shao was then at the West Province duty quarters. That very night he warned all the bureaus: "The great army is about to launch a major campaign — each of you should ready boats, ships, and storehouses; have everything prepared by dawn.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Fan was executed, Shao was then on duty at the West Province quarters. That very night he warned all the bureaus: "The great army is about to launch a major campaign — each of you should ready boats, ships, and storehouses, and have everything prepared by dawn.

sentences.zh: 」旦日，帝求諸簿署，應時即至；

translations.literal: " The next morning the Emperor called for the various registers and offices, and they were delivered at once;
translations.idiomatic: The next morning the Emperor called for the various registers and offices, and they were delivered at once;

sentences.zh: 怪問其速，諸曹答曰：「昨夜受張主簿處分。

translations.literal: astonished, he asked how they had come so quickly; the bureaus answered: "Last night we received Chief Clerk Zhang's orders.
translations.idiomatic: Astonished, he asked how they had come so quickly; the bureaus answered: "Last night we received Chief Clerk Zhang's orders.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「張邵可謂同我憂慮矣。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Zhang Shao may truly be said to share my anxieties.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Zhang Shao may truly be said to share my anxieties.

sentences.zh: 」九年，世子始開征虜府，補邵錄事參軍，轉號中軍，遷諮議參軍，領記室。

translations.literal: " In the ninth year, when the Crown Prince first opened the office of the General Who Campaigns Against Captives, Shao was appointed Recording Officer; his title was changed to Central Army, then he was promoted to Advisory Officer and put in charge of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when the Crown Prince first opened the office of the General Who Campaigns Against Captives, Shao was appointed Recording Officer; his title was changed to Central Army, then he was promoted to Advisory Officer and put in charge of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十二年，武帝北伐，邵請見，曰：「人生危脆，必當遠慮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, during Emperor Wu's northern campaign, Shao requested an audience and said: "Human life is fragile and precarious — one must plan far ahead.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, during Emperor Wu's northern campaign, Shao requested an audience and said: "Human life is fragile and precarious — one must plan far ahead.

sentences.zh: 穆之若邂逅不幸，誰可代之？

translations.literal: If Muzhi should meet with unexpected misfortune, who could replace him?
translations.idiomatic: If Muzhi should meet with unexpected misfortune, who could replace him?

sentences.zh: 尊業如此，苟有不諱，事將如何？

translations.literal: Your great enterprise stands as it does; if anything should befall you, how will affairs proceed?
translations.idiomatic: Your great enterprise stands as it does; if anything should befall you, how will affairs proceed?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「此自委穆之及卿耳。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "That I entrust to Muzhi and to you.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "That I entrust to Muzhi and to you.

sentences.zh: 」青州刺史檀祗鎮廣陵，時滁州結聚亡命，祗率眾掩之。

translations.literal: " The Inspector of Qing Province, Tan Zhi, was stationed at Guangling. At the time fugitives had gathered at Chuzhou, and Zhi led troops to take them by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: The Inspector of Qing Province, Tan Zhi, was stationed at Guangling. At the time fugitives had gathered at Chuzhou, and Zhi led troops to take them by surprise.

sentences.zh: 劉穆之恐以為變，將發軍。

translations.literal: Liu Muzhi feared this might become a rebellion and was about to dispatch troops.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi feared this might spark a rebellion and was about to dispatch troops.

sentences.zh: 邵曰：「檀韶據中流，道濟為軍首，若疑狀發露，恐生大變。

translations.literal: Shao said: "Tan Shao holds the middle Yangtze, and Dao Ji is chief of the army — if suspicions are exposed, I fear a great upheaval may arise.
translations.idiomatic: Shao said: "Tan Shao holds the middle Yangtze, and Dao Ji is chief of the army — if suspicions are exposed, I fear a great upheaval may arise.

sentences.zh: 宜且遣慰勞，以觀其意。

translations.literal: It would be best first to send envoys to console and reassure them, and observe their intentions.
translations.idiomatic: It would be best first to send envoys to console and reassure them, and observe their intentions.

sentences.zh: 」既而祗果不動。

translations.literal: " Before long Zhi indeed made no move.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhi indeed made no move.

sentences.zh: 及穆之卒，朝廷恇懼，便欲發詔以司馬徐羨之代之，邵對曰：「今誠急病，任終在徐，且世子無專命，宜須北咨。

translations.literal: When Muzhi died, the court was filled with alarm and wanted at once to issue an edict appointing Marshal Xu Xianzhi to replace him. Shao replied: "Though the situation is truly urgent, the appointment ultimately belongs to Xu — and moreover the Crown Prince has no authority to act on his own; we should first consult the north.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzhi died, the court was filled with alarm and wanted at once to issue an edict appointing Marshal Xu Xianzhi to replace him. Shao replied: "Though the situation is truly urgent, the appointment ultimately belongs to Xu — and moreover the Crown Prince has no authority to act on his own; we should first consult the north.

sentences.zh: 」信反，方使世子出命曰：「朝廷及大府事，悉咨徐司馬，其餘啟還。

translations.literal: " When the messenger returned, only then did they have the Crown Prince issue an order: "In matters of the court and the grand office, consult Marshal Xu on all points; report back on everything else.
translations.idiomatic: When the messenger returned, only then did they have the Crown Prince issue an order: "In matters of the court and the grand office, consult Marshal Xu on all points; report back on everything else.

sentences.zh: 」武帝重其臨事不撓，有大臣體。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wu valued his steadfastness in action and his bearing as a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu valued his steadfastness in action and his bearing as a great minister.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以世子鎮荊州，邵諫曰：「儲貳之重，四海所係，不宜處外，敢以死請。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, when the Crown Prince was to garrison Jing Province, Shao remonstrated: "The heir apparent bears weight on which all within the four seas depend — he should not be stationed abroad. I venture to plead with my life.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, when the Crown Prince was to garrison Jing Province, Shao remonstrated: "The heir apparent bears weight on which all within the four seas depend — he should not be stationed abroad. I venture to plead with my life.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor heeded him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor heeded him.

sentences.zh: 文帝為中郎將、荊州刺史，以邵為司馬，領南郡相，眾事悉決於邵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen served as General of the Guard and Inspector of Jing Province, he appointed Shao as Marshal and concurrent Administrator of Nan Commandery; all affairs were decided by Shao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen served as General of the Guard and Inspector of Jing Province, he appointed Shao as Marshal and concurrent Administrator of Nan Commandery; all affairs were decided by Shao.

sentences.zh: 武帝受命，以佐命功，封臨沮伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the Mandate, Shao was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linju for his founding service.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu received the Mandate, Shao was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linju for his founding service.

sentences.zh: 分荊州立湘州，以邵為刺史。

translations.literal: Jing Province was divided to establish Xiang Province, and Shao was appointed its Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Province was divided to establish Xiang Province, and Shao was appointed its Inspector.

sentences.zh: 將署府，邵以為長沙內地，非用武之國，置署妨人，乖為政要。

translations.literal: When offices were about to be established there, Shao argued that the interior of Changsha was no country for military deployment — setting up a command would hinder the people and run against the essentials of governance.
translations.idiomatic: When offices were about to be established there, Shao argued that the interior of Changsha was no country for military deployment — setting up a command would burden the people and run against the essentials of governance.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 謝晦反，遺書要邵，邵不發函，馳使呈帝。

translations.literal: When Xie Hui rebelled, he sent a letter inviting Shao to join; Shao did not open the envelope but sent a messenger posthaste to present it to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Hui rebelled, he sent a letter inviting Shao to join; Shao did not open the envelope but sent a messenger posthaste to present it to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 元嘉五年，轉征虜將軍，領寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to General Who Subdues Barbarians, concurrently Colonel Who Pacifies Barbarians and Inspector of Yong Province, with added status as Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to General Who Subdues Barbarians, concurrently Colonel Who Pacifies Barbarians and Inspector of Yong Province, with added status as Area Commander.

sentences.zh: 初，王華與邵有隙，及華參要，親舊為之危心。

translations.literal: Earlier Wang Hua and Shao had been at odds; when Hua took part in important affairs, relatives and friends feared for Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Hua and Shao had been at odds; when Hua took part in important affairs, relatives and friends feared for Shao.

sentences.zh: 邵曰：「子陵方弘至公，必不以私仇害正義。

translations.literal: Shao said: "Ziling is now extending the highest fairness — he will certainly not let a private grudge harm what is right.
translations.idiomatic: Shao said: "Ziling is now extending the highest fairness — he will certainly not let a private grudge harm what is right.

sentences.zh: 」是任也，華實舉之。

translations.literal: " As it turned out, Hua himself recommended him for the post.
translations.idiomatic: As it turned out, Hua himself recommended him for the post.

sentences.zh: 及至襄陽，築長圍，修立堤堰，開田數千頃，郡人賴之富贍。

translations.literal: When he reached Xiangyang, he built a long encirclement wall, constructed dikes and weirs, and opened fields of several thousand qing; the people of the commandery relied on this and grew prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Xiangyang, he built a long encirclement wall, constructed dikes and weirs, and opened fields of several thousand qing; the people of the commandery relied on this and grew prosperous.

sentences.zh: 丹、淅二川蠻屢為寇，邵誘其帥，因大會誅之，悉掩其徒黨。

translations.literal: The barbarians along the Dan and Xi rivers had repeatedly raided. Shao lured their chiefs and, at a great assembly, executed them, then swept up all their followers.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians along the Dan and Xi rivers had repeatedly raided. Shao lured their chiefs and, at a great assembly, executed them, then swept up all their followers.

sentences.zh: 既失信群蠻，所在並起，水陸斷絕。

translations.literal: Having forfeited the trust of the barbarian groups, they rose everywhere at once, and land and water routes were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Having forfeited the trust of the barbarian groups, they rose everywhere at once, and land and water routes were cut off.

sentences.zh: 子敷至襄陽定省，當還都，群蠻伺欲取之。

translations.literal: His son Fu came to Xiangyang to visit his parents and was about to return to the capital; the barbarians watched for an opportunity to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu came to Xiangyang to visit his parents and was about to return to the capital; the barbarians watched for an opportunity to seize him.

sentences.zh: 會蠕蠕國遣使朝貢，賊以為敷，遂執之，邵坐降號揚烈將軍。

translations.literal: It happened that Rouran sent envoys with tribute; the bandits took them for Fu's party and seized them. Shao was demoted to General Who Raises Martial Valor for the fault.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Rouran sent envoys with tribute; the bandits took them for Fu's party and seized them. Shao was demoted to General Who Raises Martial Valor for the fault.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭鎮江陵，以邵為撫軍長史，持節、南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, garrisoned Jiangling, he appointed Shao Chief of Staff to the Pacifying Army, with staff of authority as Colonel of Southern Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, garrisoned Jiangling, he appointed Shao Chief of Staff to the Pacifying Army, with staff of authority as Colonel of Southern Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 坐在雍州營私蓄取贓貨二百四十五萬，下廷尉，免官，削爵土。

translations.literal: He was convicted of private profiteering while in Yong Province and amassing bribes of 2.45 million; he was sent to the Minister of Justice, dismissed from office, and stripped of title and fief.
translations.idiomatic: He was convicted of private profiteering while in Yong Province and amassing bribes of 2.45 million; he was sent to the Minister of Justice, dismissed from office, and stripped of title and fief.

sentences.zh: 後為吳興太守，卒，追復爵邑，諡曰簡伯。

translations.literal: Later he served as Administrator of Wu Xing; he died, and his title and fief were posthumously restored. His posthumous title was Marquis Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Administrator of Wu Xing; he died, and his title and fief were posthumously restored. His posthumous title was Marquis Jian.

sentences.zh: 邵臨終，遺命祭以菜果，葦席為轜車，諸子從焉。

translations.literal: As Shao lay dying, he left instructions that sacrifices be offered with vegetables and fruit only, and that a reed mat serve as his bier; his sons complied.
translations.idiomatic: As Shao lay dying, he left instructions that sacrifices be offered with vegetables and fruit only, and that a reed mat serve as his bier; his sons complied.

sentences.zh: 子敷、演、鏡，有名於世。

translations.literal: His sons Fu, Yan, and Jing were renowned in their time.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Fu, Yan, and Jing were renowned in their time.

sentences.zh: 敷字景胤。

translations.literal: Fu, styled Jingyin.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, styled Jingyin.

sentences.zh: 生而母亡，年數歲，問知之，雖童蒙，便有感慕之色。

translations.literal: His mother died when he was born; when he was only a few years old and learned of it, though still a small child he already showed the look of longing and grief.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died when he was born; when he was only a few years old and learned of it, though still a small child he already showed the look of longing and grief.

sentences.zh: 至十歲許，求母遺物，而散施已盡，唯得一扇，乃緘錄之。

translations.literal: At about ten he sought his mother's keepsakes, but they had all been given away in charity; he obtained only a fan, which he sealed away and preserved.
translations.idiomatic: At about ten he sought his mother's keepsakes, but they had all been given away in charity; he obtained only a fan, which he sealed away and preserved.

sentences.zh: 每至感思，輒開笥流涕。

translations.literal: Whenever remembrance overcame him, he would open the box and weep.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever remembrance overcame him, he would open the box and weep.

sentences.zh: 見從母，悲戚嗚咽。

translations.literal: When he saw his aunt, he grieved and sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw his aunt, he grieved and sobbed.

sentences.zh: 性整貴，風韻端雅，好玄言，善屬文。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright and noble; his bearing was refined and graceful. He loved metaphysical discourse and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and noble; his bearing was refined and graceful. He loved metaphysical discourse and was skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 初，父邵使與南陽宗少文談《繫》、《象》，往復數番，少文每欲屈，握麈尾歎曰：「吾道東矣。

translations.literal: At first his father Shao had him discuss the Appended Remarks and the Images with Zong Shaowen of Nanyang. After several exchanges, Shaowen was repeatedly on the verge of defeat; gripping his fly-whisk, he sighed: "My Way has gone east.
translations.idiomatic: At first his father Shao had him discuss the Appended Remarks and the Images with Zong Shaowen of Nanyang. After several exchanges, Shaowen was repeatedly on the verge of defeat; gripping his fly-whisk, he sighed: "My Way has gone east.

sentences.zh: 」於是名價日重。

translations.literal: " From then on Fu's reputation and esteem grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Fu's reputation and esteem grew daily.

sentences.zh: 武帝聞其美，召見奇之，曰：「真千里駒也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu heard of his excellence, summoned him, and found him remarkable, saying: "Truly a thousand-li colt.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu heard of his excellence, summoned him, and found him remarkable, saying: "Truly a thousand-li colt.

sentences.zh: 」以為世子中軍參軍，數見接引。

translations.literal: " He was appointed Staff Officer of the Crown Prince's Central Army and was often received and guided by the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Staff Officer of the Crown Prince's Central Army and was often received and guided by the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 累遷江夏王義恭撫軍記室參軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Recording Officer on the staff of the Pacifying Army under the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly to Recording Officer on the staff of the Pacifying Army under the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong.

sentences.zh: 義恭就文帝求一學義沙門，會敷赴假江陵，入辭，文帝令以後車載沙門往，謂曰：「道中可得言晤。

translations.literal: Yigong asked Emperor Wen for a monk learned in doctrine. It happened that Fu was on leave en route to Jiangling; when he came to take leave, Emperor Wen ordered the monk carried in the rear carriage and said: "On the road you two may converse and meet.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong asked Emperor Wen for a monk learned in doctrine. It happened that Fu was on leave en route to Jiangling; when he came to take leave, Emperor Wen ordered the monk carried in the rear carriage and said: "On the road you two may converse and meet.

sentences.zh: 」敷不奉詔，上甚不說。

translations.literal: " Fu did not obey the edict, and the sovereign was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Fu did not obey the edict, and the sovereign was greatly displeased.

sentences.zh: 遷正員中書郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Regular Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Regular Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 敷小名查，父邵小名梨，文帝戲之曰：「查何如梨？

translations.literal: Fu's childhood name was Cha and his father Shao's was Li. Emperor Wen teased him: "How does Cha compare with Li?
translations.idiomatic: Fu's childhood name was Cha and his father Shao's was Li. Emperor Wen teased him: "How does Cha compare with Li?

sentences.zh: 」敷曰：「梨為百果之宗，查何可比。」

translations.literal: " Fu said: "The pear is sovereign among all fruits — how can Cha be compared?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu said: "The pear is sovereign among all fruits — how can Cha be compared?"

sentences.zh: 中書舍人狄當、周赳並管要務，以敷同省名家，欲詣之。

translations.literal: The Secretariat Attendants Di Dang and Zhou Qiu both managed important affairs; because Fu was from a distinguished family in the same department, they wished to call on him.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat Attendants Di Dang and Zhou Qiu both managed important affairs; because Fu was from a distinguished family in the same department, they wished to call on him.

sentences.zh: 赳曰：「彼恐不相容接，不如勿往。

translations.literal: Qiu said: "He probably will not receive us — better not go.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu said: "He probably will not receive us — better not go.

sentences.zh: 」當曰：「吾等並已員外郎矣，何憂不得共坐。

translations.literal: " Dang said: "We are already supplementary gentlemen — why worry that we cannot sit together?
translations.idiomatic: Dang said: "We are already supplementary gentlemen — why worry that we cannot sit together?

sentences.zh: 」敷先設二床，去壁三四尺，二客就席，敷呼左右曰：「移我遠客！

translations.literal: " Fu had two beds set out three or four chi from the wall. When the two guests took their seats, Fu called to his attendants: "Move my distant guests farther away!
translations.idiomatic: Fu had two beds set out three or four chi from the wall. When the two guests took their seats, Fu called to his attendants: "Move my distant guests farther away!

sentences.zh: 」赳等失色而去。

translations.literal: " Qiu and the others turned pale and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu and the others turned pale and departed.

sentences.zh: 其自標遇如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he held himself.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he held himself.

sentences.zh: 善持音儀，盡詳緩之致，與人別，執手曰：「念相聞。

translations.literal: He was skilled at maintaining tone and bearing, achieving to the full the quality of leisurely grace; when parting from others he would clasp their hands and say: "Think of me when you hear word of me.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at maintaining tone and bearing, achieving to the full the quality of leisurely grace; when parting from others he would clasp their hands and say: "Think of me when you hear word of me.

sentences.zh: 」餘響久之不絕。

translations.literal: " The resonance of his words lingered long after.
translations.idiomatic: The resonance of his words lingered long after.

sentences.zh: 張氏後進皆慕之，其源起自敷也。

translations.literal: The younger members of the Zhang clan all admired this; its source began with Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The younger members of the Zhang clan all admired this; its source began with Fu.

sentences.zh: 遷黃門侍郎、始興王濬後將軍司徒左長史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and Left Chief Clerk to the Secretariat under the Rear General, Prince of Shixing Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and Left Chief Clerk to the Secretariat under the Rear General, Prince of Shixing Jun.

sentences.zh: 未拜，父在吳興亡，成服凡十餘日，方進水漿，葬畢，不進鹽菜，遂毀瘠成疾。

translations.literal: Before he could assume office, his father died in Wu Xing. He wore mourning garments for more than ten days before taking even water or gruel; after the burial he ate no salt or vegetables, and thus wasted away into illness.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume office, his father died in Wu Xing. He wore mourning garments for more than ten days before taking even water or gruel; after the burial he ate no salt or vegetables, and thus wasted away into illness.

sentences.zh: 伯父茂度每譬止之，敷益更感慟，絕而復續。

translations.literal: His uncle Maodu repeatedly admonished him to stop, but Fu only grieved the more deeply, fainting and reviving.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Maodu repeatedly admonished him to stop, but Fu only grieved the more deeply, fainting and reviving.

sentences.zh: 茂度曰：「我比止汝，而乃益甚。

translations.literal: Maodu said: "I came to stop you, and yet you only grow worse.
translations.idiomatic: Maodu said: "I came to stop you, and yet you only grow worse.

sentences.zh: 」自是不復往，未期年而卒。

translations.literal: " From then on he never visited again; before a full year had passed, Fu died.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he never visited again; before a full year had passed, Fu died.

sentences.zh: 孝武即位，旌其孝道，追贈侍中，改其所居為孝張里。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, he commended Fu's filial devotion, posthumously granted him Attendant-in-Ordinary, and renamed his residence Filial Zhang Lane.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, he commended Fu's filial devotion, posthumously granted him Attendant-in-Ordinary, and renamed his residence Filial Zhang Lane.

sentences.zh: 敷弟柬，襲父封，位通直郎。

translations.literal: Fu's younger brother Dong inherited their father's enfeoffment and held the post of Direct-and-Upright Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's younger brother Dong inherited their father's enfeoffment and held the post of Direct-and-Upright Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 柬有勇力，手格猛獸，元兇以為輔國將軍。

translations.literal: Dong had courage and strength and could grapple fierce beasts bare-handed; Yuan Xiong appointed him Assistant State General.
translations.idiomatic: Dong had courage and strength and could grapple fierce beasts bare-handed; Yuan Xiong appointed him Assistant State General.

sentences.zh: 孝武至新亭，柬出奔，墜淮死。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Xinting, Dong fled and fell into the Huai River and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Xinting, Dong fled and fell into the Huai River and drowned.

sentences.zh: 子式嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shi succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 暢字少微，邵兄偉之子也。

translations.literal: Chang, styled Shaowei, was the son of Shao's elder brother Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, styled Shaowei, was the son of Shao's elder brother Wei.

sentences.zh: 偉少有操行，為晉琅邪王國郎中令，從王至洛，還京都，武帝封藥酒一罌付偉，令密加鴆毒，受命於道，自飲而卒。

translations.literal: Wei from youth had integrity of conduct; he served as Chief Commandant of Palace Attendants in the Kingdom of Langya under Jin. When he followed the prince to Luoyang and returned to the capital, Emperor Wu sealed a jar of medicinal wine and entrusted it to Wei, ordering him secretly to add poison; Wei received the order on the road, drank it himself, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Wei from youth had integrity of conduct; he served as Chief Commandant of Palace Attendants in the Kingdom of Langya under Jin. When he followed the prince to Luoyang and returned to the capital, Emperor Wu sealed a jar of medicinal wine and entrusted it to Wei, ordering him secretly to add poison; Wei received the order on the road, drank it himself, and died.

sentences.zh: 暢少與從兄敷、演、鏡齊名，為後進之秀。

translations.literal: Chang in youth shared renown with his cousins Fu, Yan, and Jing, and was outstanding among the rising generation.
translations.idiomatic: Chang in youth shared renown with his cousins Fu, Yan, and Jing, and was outstanding among the rising generation.

sentences.zh: 起家為太守徐佩之主簿，佩之被誅，暢馳出奔赴，制服盡哀，時論美之。

translations.literal: He began his career as Chief Clerk to Administrator Xu Peizhi; when Peizhi was executed, Chang galloped out to attend the body, donned mourning and grieved to the full — contemporaries praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Chief Clerk to Administrator Xu Peizhi; when Peizhi was executed, Chang galloped out to attend the body, donned mourning and grieved to the full — contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 弟牧嘗為猘犬所傷，醫者云食蝦蟇可療，牧難之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Mu was once bitten by a mad dog; the physician said eating toads could cure it, but Mu balked at the remedy.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Mu was once bitten by a mad dog; the physician said eating toads could cure it, but Mu balked at the remedy.

sentences.zh: 暢含笑先嘗，牧因此乃食，由是遂愈。

translations.literal: Chang smiled, tasted first himself; Mu thereupon ate, and by this was healed.
translations.idiomatic: Chang smiled and tasted the toads first; only then did Mu eat, and he recovered.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Crown Prince Vice-Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Crown Prince Vice-Councillor.

sentences.zh: 孝武鎮彭城，暢為安北長史、沛郡太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu was stationed at Pengcheng, Chang served as Chief Clerk to the General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Pei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Xiaowu held Pengcheng, Chang was Chief Clerk to the General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Pei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年，魏主托跋燾南征，太尉江夏王義恭統諸軍出鎮彭城。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, the Wei ruler Tuoba Tao marched south on campaign; Grand Commandant the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, took command of the armies and went out to garrison Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia twenty-seven the Wei ruler Tuoba Tao marched south; Grand Commandant Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, took overall command and moved out to garrison Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 虜眾近城數十里，彭城眾力雖多，而軍食不足，義恭欲棄彭城南歸，計議彌日不定。

translations.literal: The barbarian host drew within several tens of li of the city. Though Pengcheng's forces were many, military provisions were insufficient; Yigong wished to abandon Pengcheng and return south, yet deliberation went on for days without decision.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy drew to within a few dozen li of the walls. Pengcheng had numbers enough, but grain for the army ran short; Yigong wanted to abandon the city and flee south, and for days the council could not settle on a plan.

sentences.zh: 時歷城眾少食多，安北中兵參軍沈慶之議欲以車營為函箱陣，精兵為外翼，奉二王及妃媛直趨歷城，分城兵配護軍將軍蕭思話留守。

translations.literal: At the time Licheng had few troops but ample food. Shen Qingzhi, Middle Army Staff Officer to the General Who Pacifies the North, proposed forming the wagon camp into a boxcar formation with elite troops as outer wings, escorting the two princes and their consorts straight to Licheng, while assigning city troops to Defensive Corps General Xiao Sihua to hold the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Licheng then had little force but plenty of food. Shen Qingzhi, middle army staff officer to the Pacifying North command, urged a wagon-fort formation: elite troops as outer wings, the two princes and their ladies rushed straight to Licheng, and the city garrison split off under Defensive Corps General Xiao Sihua to hold Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 太尉長史何勖不同，欲席捲奔鬱洲，自海道還都。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Chief Clerk He Xu disagreed, wishing to sweep everything along in flight to Yuzhou and return to the capital by sea.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Chief Clerk He Xu dissented: he wanted to pack up and bolt for Yuzhou, then take the sea route home.

sentences.zh: 二議未決，更集群僚議之。

translations.literal: The two proposals unsettled, they gathered the staff officials again to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: With the two plans still unresolved, they convened the staff once more.

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「若歷城、鬱洲可至，下官敢不高贊。

translations.literal: Chang said: "If Licheng and Yuzhou can be reached, your humble servant would not dare fail to give his full approval.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said: "If Licheng and Yuzhou were truly within reach, I would be the first to applaud.

sentences.zh: 今城內乏食，人無固心，但以關扃嚴密，不獲走耳。

translations.literal: Now food within the city is scarce and the people have no firm heart; it is only because the gates are barred so strictly that they cannot flee.
translations.idiomatic: Food inside the walls is low and hearts are unsteady; men stay only because the gates are locked tight and there is nowhere to run.

sentences.zh: 若一搖動，則潰然奔散，雖欲至所在，其可得乎！

translations.literal: If once stirred, they would collapse and scatter in flight — even if one wished to reach the destination, how could it be done!
translations.idiomatic: Stir them once and they will break and flee in panic — even if you mean to reach your goal, how could you?

sentences.zh: 今食雖寡，然朝夕未至窘乏，豈可舍萬全之術，而即危亡之道。

translations.literal: Though food is now scant, morning and evening we have not yet reached desperate want — how can we abandon a method of complete safety and rush straight toward peril and ruin!
translations.idiomatic: Provisions are thin, yes, but we are not yet starving day to day. Why cast aside a course that still keeps us whole and choose the road to ruin?

sentences.zh: 此計必行，下官請以頸血污君馬跡！

translations.literal: If this plan is carried out, your humble servant asks to stain Your Lordship's horse's tracks with the blood of his neck!
translations.idiomatic: If you take this road, I ask only to die under your horse's hooves!

sentences.zh: 」孝武聞暢議，謂義恭曰：「張長史言，不可違也。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Xiaowu heard Chang's argument, he said to Yigong: "What Chief Clerk Zhang says must not be disobeyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu heard Chang, he told Yigong: "Chief Clerk Zhang is right — do not go against him.

sentences.zh: 」義恭乃止。

translations.literal: " Yigong then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 魏主既至，登城南亞父塚，於戲馬臺立氈屋。

translations.literal: When the Wei ruler arrived, he ascended Ya Fu's mound south of the city and erected a felt tent on the Playhorse Platform.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Wei ruler arrived, he climbed Ya Fu's tomb south of the city and pitched a felt pavilion on the Playhorse Platform.

sentences.zh: 先是，隊主蒯應見執，其日晡時，遣送應至小市門，致意求甘蔗及酒。

translations.literal: Earlier, squad leader Kuai Ying had been captured; that day at the hour of shen, they sent Ying to the Small Market Gate with a message requesting sugarcane and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, squad leader Kuai Ying had been taken prisoner; that afternoon they sent him to the Small Market Gate with a request for sugarcane and wine.

sentences.zh: 孝武遣送酒二器，甘蔗百挺。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu sent two jars of wine and a hundred stalks of sugarcane.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu sent two jars of wine and a hundred stalks of sugarcane.

sentences.zh: 求駱駝。

translations.literal: They requested a camel.
translations.idiomatic: They asked for a camel.

sentences.zh: 明日，魏主又自上戲馬臺，復遣使至小市門，求與孝武相見，遣送駱駝，並致雜物，使於南門受之。

translations.literal: The next day the Wei ruler again ascended the Playhorse Platform himself and once more sent envoys to the Small Market Gate, requesting to meet Emperor Xiaowu; they sent a camel and also presented various goods, directing that they be received at the South Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Wei ruler again mounted the Playhorse Platform and sent envoys to the Small Market Gate asking to meet Emperor Xiaowu; they delivered a camel and other gifts, to be received at the South Gate.

sentences.zh: 暢於城上與魏尚書李孝伯語，孝伯問：「君何姓？

translations.literal: On the wall Chang conversed with Wei Minister of the Masters of Writing Li Xiaobo. Xiaobo asked: "What is your surname?
translations.idiomatic: From the ramparts Chang spoke with Li Xiaobo, Minister of the Masters of Writing of Wei. Xiaobo asked: "What is your surname?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「姓張。

translations.literal: " He answered: "Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Zhang.

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「張長史乎？

translations.literal: " Xiaobo said: "Chief Clerk Zhang?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said: "Chief Clerk Zhang?

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「君何得見識？

translations.literal: " Chang said: "How do you recognize me?
translations.idiomatic: Chang said: "How do you know me?

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「君名聲遠聞，足使我知。

translations.literal: " Xiaobo said: "Your renown has spread far — enough for me to know.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said: "Your name carries far — that is enough for me to know.

sentences.zh: 」城內有具思者，嘗在魏，義恭使視，知是孝伯，乃開門餉物。

translations.literal: " Within the city was one Ju Si, who had once served in Wei; Yigong sent him to look, recognized that it was Xiaobo, and opened the gate to supply goods.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the city was Ju Si, who had once served Wei; Yigong sent him to look and, recognizing Xiaobo, opened the gate to send provisions.

sentences.zh: 魏主又求酒及甘橘，孝武又致螺杯雜物，南土所珍。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler again requested wine and sweet oranges; Emperor Xiaowu in turn sent spiral-shell cups and various goods prized in the southern lands.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler asked again for wine and sweet oranges; Emperor Xiaowu replied with conch cups and other treasures of the south.

sentences.zh: 魏主復令孝伯傳語曰：「魏主有詔借博具。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler again had Xiaobo relay a message: "The Wei ruler has an edict to borrow gaming implements.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler had Xiaobo pass word: "The Wei ruler decrees that gaming pieces be lent.

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「博具當為申致，有詔之言，正可施於彼國，何得施之於此？

translations.literal: " Chang said: "The gaming implements shall be conveyed on request — but talk of 'edicts' applies properly to that state; how can it be applied here?
translations.idiomatic: Chang said: "We can relay a request for gaming pieces — but an 'edict' belongs to your realm; how can it be spoken here?

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「以鄰國之臣耳。

translations.literal: " Xiaobo said: "As a minister of a neighboring state, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said: "I speak only as a minister of a neighboring state.

sentences.zh: 」孝伯又言：「太尉、鎮軍，久闕南信，殊當憂邑。

translations.literal: " Xiaobo spoke again: "The Grand Commandant and the Pacifying Army General have long lacked word from the south — they must be deeply anxious.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo added: "The Grand Commandant and the Pacifying Army General have had no news from the south for so long — they must be sick with worry.

sentences.zh: 若遣信，當為護送。

translations.literal: If you send messengers, we shall escort them.
translations.idiomatic: Send couriers and we will see them safely through.

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「此中間道甚多，亦不須煩魏。

translations.literal: " Chang said: "There are many routes in between; there is no need to trouble Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said: "There are plenty of paths between us; we need not trouble Wei.

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「亦知有水路，似為白賊所斷。

translations.literal: " Xiaobo said: "We know there is also a water route — but it seems cut off by White Bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said: "We know the water road too — but the White Bandits seem to have cut it.

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「君著白衣，故號白賊也。

translations.literal: " Chang said: "You wear white robes — hence the name White Bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said: "You dress in white — that is why they are called White Bandits.

sentences.zh: 」孝伯笑曰：「今之白賊，亦不異黃巾、赤眉，但不在江南耳。

translations.literal: " Xiaobo laughed and said: "Today's White Bandits differ little from the Yellow Turbans and Red Eyebrows — only they are not in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo laughed: "Today's White Bandits are no different from the Yellow Turbans and Red Eyebrows — only they are not in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 」又求博具，俄送與。

translations.literal: " They requested gaming implements again, and soon they were sent.
translations.idiomatic: They asked again for gaming pieces, and soon received them.

sentences.zh: 魏主又遣送氈及九種鹽並胡豉，云：「此諸鹽，各有宜。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler again sent felt rugs, nine kinds of salt, and Hu fermented beans, saying: "Each of these salts has its proper use.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler sent felt, nine kinds of salt, and Hu fermented beans, saying: "Each salt has its use.

sentences.zh: 白鹽是魏主所食；

translations.literal: White salt is what the Wei ruler eats;
translations.idiomatic: White salt is the Wei ruler's table salt;

sentences.zh: 黑者療腹脹氣滿，刮取六銖，以酒服之；

translations.literal: black treats abdominal distension and gas fullness — scrape off six zhu and take it with wine;
translations.idiomatic: black salt treats bloating and gas — scrape six zhu and take it in wine;

sentences.zh: 胡鹽療目痛。

translations.literal: Hu salt treats eye pain.
translations.idiomatic: Hu salt treats sore eyes.

sentences.zh: 柔鹽不用食，療馬脊創；

translations.literal: soft salt is not for eating — it treats wounds on a horse's spine;
translations.idiomatic: soft salt is not eaten; it heals wounds along a horse's back;

sentences.zh: 赤鹽、駁鹽、臭鹽、馬齒鹽四種，並不中食。

translations.literal: red salt, mottled salt, foul salt, and horsetooth salt — four kinds — are all unfit for food.
translations.idiomatic: red, mottled, foul, and horsetooth salt — four kinds — are not fit to eat.

sentences.zh: 胡豉亦中啖。

translations.literal: Hu fermented beans are also suitable to eat.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu fermented beans may be eaten as well.

sentences.zh: 」又求黃甘，並云：「魏主致意太尉、安北，何不遣人來問，觀我儀貌，察我為人。
