translations.literal: " They again requested yellow citrus and also said: "The Wei ruler sends greetings to the Grand Commandant and the General Who Pacifies the North — why not send someone to inquire after him, observe his bearing, and gauge his character?
translations.idiomatic: They asked again for sweet oranges and added: "The Wei ruler sends regards to the Grand Commandant and the Pacifying North commander — why not send someone to visit, see his bearing, and learn his character?

sentences.zh: 」暢又宣旨答曰：「魏主形狀才力，久為來往所見。

translations.literal: " Chang again proclaimed the reply: "The Wei ruler's form and talents have long been observed in our exchanges.
translations.idiomatic: Chang answered in turn: "The Wei ruler's looks and strength have been plain enough in all our back-and-forth.

sentences.zh: 李尚書親自銜命，不忍彼此不盡，故不復遣。

translations.literal: Minister Li has personally borne his commission — unwilling that either side fail in courtesy, we shall not send anyone again.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Li has come in person; we would not have either side stint in courtesy — so we need not send anyone else.

sentences.zh: 」又云「魏主恨向所送馬殊不稱意，安北若須大馬，當送之，脫須蜀馬，亦有佳者。

translations.literal: " It was further said: "The Wei ruler resents that the horses sent earlier were quite unsatisfactory — if the General Who Pacifies the North needs large horses, they will be sent; if perchance he needs Shu horses, fine ones are available too.
translations.idiomatic: They added: "The Wei ruler was displeased with the horses sent before — if the Pacifying North commander wants tall horses, we will send them; if he prefers Shu mounts, we have good ones too.

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「安北不乏良駟，送在彼意，此非所求。

translations.literal: " Chang said: "The General Who Pacifies the North lacks no fine steeds — the sending is in your good will; this is not what we seek.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said: "The Pacifying North commander lacks no fine horses; your gift is kind, but it is not what we asked for.

sentences.zh: 」義恭又送炬燭十挺，孝武亦致錦一匹。

translations.literal: " Yigong also sent ten bundles of torch-candles, and Emperor Xiaowu sent a bolt of brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong sent ten bundles of torch-candles; Emperor Xiaowu sent a bolt of brocade.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「知更須黃甘，若給彼軍，即不能足；

translations.literal: He further said: "Knowing you need yellow citrus again — if supplied to your army, it cannot suffice;
translations.idiomatic: He added: "We know you want more sweet oranges — if we fed your whole army, we could not fill the need;

sentences.zh: 若供魏主，未當乏絕，故不復致。

translations.literal: if supplied to the Wei ruler alone, there would be no lack — therefore we send no more.
translations.idiomatic: but for the Wei ruler alone we would not run short — so we send no more.

sentences.zh: 」孝伯又曰：「君南土膏粱，何為著屩？

translations.literal: " Xiaobo again said: "You are southern gentry — why wear straw sandals?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said again: "You are southern nobility — why wear straw sandals?

sentences.zh: 君且如此，將士云何？

translations.literal: If you dress thus, what of your officers and soldiers?
translations.idiomatic: If even you go like this, what of your officers and men?

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「膏粱之言，誠以為愧。

translations.literal: " Chang said: "Your words of gentry upbringing do indeed shame me.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said: "Your talk of noble breeding does shame me.

sentences.zh: 但以不武，受命統軍，戎陣軍間，不容緩服。

translations.literal: Yet being no warrior, yet charged to command armies — in camp and battle line one cannot wear leisurely dress.
translations.idiomatic: But I am no fighter, yet I was ordered to command an army — in camp and on the field one cannot dress at ease.

sentences.zh: 」魏主又遣就二王借箜篌、琵琶等器及棋子，孝伯足詞辯，亦北土之美。

translations.literal: " The Wei ruler again sent envoys to borrow from the two princes the konghou, pipa, and other instruments plus chess pieces. Xiaobo was fully gifted in rhetoric — a northern paragon as well.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler sent again to borrow from the two princes the konghou, pipa, and other instruments, and chess pieces. Xiaobo was quick with words — a northern wit in his own right.

sentences.zh: 暢隨宜應答，甚為敏捷，音韻詳雅，魏人美之。

translations.literal: Chang answered as occasion required, very quick and agile; his tone refined and elegant — the Wei men admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang matched him point for point, swift and supple; his diction was polished and graceful, and the northerners admired him.

sentences.zh: 時魏聲云當出襄陽，故以暢為南譙王義宣司空長史、南郡太守。

translations.literal: At the time Wei rumor said they would move against Xiangyang; therefore Chang was made Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works for the Prince of Nanqiao, Yixuan, and Administrator of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor then had Wei marching on Xiangyang, so Chang was made chief clerk to Minister of Works Yixuan, Prince of Nanqiao, and Administrator of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 元兇弑逆，義宣發哀之日，即便舉兵。

translations.literal: When Yuan Xiong committed regicide, on the day Yixuan proclaimed mourning he at once raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Xiong murdered his father, Yixuan raised an army the very day he began mourning.

sentences.zh: 暢為元佐，舉哀畢，改服著黃袴褶，出射堂簡人，音儀容止，眾皆矚目，見者皆為盡命。

translations.literal: Chang was chief aide; when mourning was finished he changed dress and donned yellow trouser-coats, went to the archery hall to select men — his voice, bearing, and demeanor drew every eye; those who saw him vowed their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was his chief aide. When mourning ended he put on yellow battle dress, went to the archery hall to choose men, and by voice and bearing held every eye; all who saw him pledged their lives.

sentences.zh: 事平，徵為吏部尚書，封夷道縣侯。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was summoned as Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yidao County.
translations.idiomatic: After the revolt was crushed he was recalled as Minister of Personnel and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yidao.

sentences.zh: 及義宣有異圖，蔡超等以暢人望，勸義宣留之，乃解南蠻校尉以授暢，加冠軍將軍，領丞相長史。

translations.literal: When Yixuan harbored divergent designs, Cai Chao and others, citing Chang's public esteem, urged Yixuan to retain him; he was relieved of the post of Commander of the Southern Barbarians and it was given to Chang, with the additional title Champion General and concurrent service as Chief Clerk to the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixuan turned toward rebellion, Cai Chao and others, valuing Chang's standing, urged Yixuan to keep him close; he stripped Chang of the Southern Barbarians command and gave it to him again with the title Champion General and concurrent chief clerk to the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 暢遣門生荀僧寶下都，因顏竣陳義宣釁狀。

translations.literal: Chang sent his student Xun Sengbao down to the capital to report Yixuan's signs of rebellion through Yan Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Chang sent his student Xun Sengbao to the capital to lay Yixuan's rebellious intent before Yan Jun.

sentences.zh: 僧寶有私貨，止巴陵不時下。

translations.literal: Sengbao had private goods and stopped at Baling, not proceeding promptly.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbao carried private merchandise and halted at Baling instead of going on at once.

sentences.zh: 會義宣起兵，津路斷絕，遂不得前。

translations.literal: Just as Yixuan raised troops, ferry routes were cut off, and he could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan then rose in arms, the river routes were severed, and Sengbao could not get through.

sentences.zh: 義宣將為逆，使嬖人翟靈寶告暢，暢陳必無此理，請以死保之。

translations.literal: As Yixuan was about to rebel, he sent his favorite Zhai Lingbao to inform Chang; Chang declared there was surely no such intent and asked to guarantee it with his life.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixuan was on the verge of rebellion he sent his favorite Zhai Lingbao to tell Chang; Chang insisted there was no such plan and offered his life as pledge.

sentences.zh: 靈寶還白義宣，云暢必不可回，請殺以徇眾，賴丞相司馬竺超民得免。

translations.literal: Lingbao returned and told Yixuan that Chang could surely not be turned — he asked to kill him to awe the masses; only thanks to Chancellor Marshal Zhu Chaomin was he spared.
translations.idiomatic: Lingbao reported back that Chang would never be swayed and asked to kill him to terrify the host; only Chancellor Marshal Zhu Chaomin saved him.

sentences.zh: 進號撫軍，別立軍部，以收人望。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to Pacifying Army General; a separate military staff was established to gather public esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted Pacifying Army General and given a separate staff, to win back popular regard.

sentences.zh: 暢雖署文檄，飲酒常醉，不省其事。

translations.literal: Though Chang signed proclamations, he drank himself constantly drunk and took no heed of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chang signed the proclamations, but drank himself drunk day after day and paid no attention to business.

sentences.zh: 及義宣敗於梁山，暢為軍人所掠，衣服都盡。

translations.literal: When Yixuan was defeated at Liangshan, Chang was plundered by soldiers and stripped of all clothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixuan fell at Liangshan, soldiers stripped Chang bare.

sentences.zh: 遇右將軍王玄謨乘輿出營，暢已得敗衣，遂排玄謨上輿，玄謨甚不悅。

translations.literal: He encountered Right General Wang Xuamo riding out in a carriage; Chang had already obtained cast-off clothes and thereupon shoved Xuamo aside and mounted the carriage — Xuamo was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He met Right General Wang Xuamo leaving camp in a carriage. Chang, having scavenged rags, shoved Xuamo aside and climbed in; Xuamo was furious.

sentences.zh: 諸將請殺之，隊主張榮救之得免。

translations.literal: The generals asked to kill him; squad leader Zhang Rong rescued him and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted him dead, but squad leader Zhang Rong saved him.

sentences.zh: 執送都下，付廷尉，見原。

translations.literal: Seized and sent to the capital, he was handed to the Court of Judicial Review and pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was taken to the capital, handed to the Court of Judicial Review, and pardoned.

sentences.zh: 起為都官尚書，轉侍中。

translations.literal: He was reappointed Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, then transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, then moved to Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 孝武宴朝賢，暢亦在坐。

translations.literal: At Emperor Xiaowu's banquet for court worthies, Chang was also among those seated.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu feasted the court's eminent men; Chang was among the guests.

sentences.zh: 何偃因醉曰：「張暢信奇才也，與義宣作賊，而卒無咎。

translations.literal: He Yan, being drunk, said: "Zhang Chang is truly a prodigy — he joined Yixuan in rebellion and yet in the end suffered no blame.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan, drunk, said: "Zhang Chang is a marvel — he made rebellion with Yixuan and still walked away unscathed.

sentences.zh: 苟非奇才，安能致此！

translations.literal: If he were not a prodigy, how could he achieve this!
translations.idiomatic: If he were not a marvel, how could that happen?

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「太初之時，誰黃其閣？

translations.literal: " Chang said: "In the Taichu era, who washed the Yellow Pavilion?
translations.idiomatic: Chang said: "In the Taichu reign, who scrubbed the Yellow Pavilion clean?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「何事相苦。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Why torment each other so.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Must you rake each other over the coals?

sentences.zh: 」初，尚之為元兇司空，及義師至新林門，人皆逃，尚之父子共洗黃閣，故暢以此譏之。

translations.literal: " Earlier, Shangzhi had served Yuan Xiong as Minister of Works; when the righteous army reached the Xinlin Gate, everyone fled — Shangzhi and his son together washed the Yellow Pavilion — hence Chang used this to mock him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shangzhi had been Minister of Works under Yuan Xiong; when the righteous army reached Xinlin Gate and all fled, Shangzhi and his son washed the Yellow Pavilion together — hence Chang's barb.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年，出為會稽太守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian he went out as Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian two he was sent out as Administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Xuan.

sentences.zh: 暢愛弟子輯，臨終遺命與輯合墳，時議非之。

translations.literal: Chang loved his nephew Ji; on his deathbed he left instructions to share a tomb with Ji — contemporaries criticized this.
translations.idiomatic: Chang adored his nephew Ji and on his deathbed ordered that they share one tomb — opinion condemned it.

sentences.zh: 弟悅，亦有美稱，歷侍中、臨海王子頊前將軍長史、南郡太守。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yue also had a fine reputation, having served as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Chief Clerk to the Vanguard General for the Prince of Linhai, Zixu, and Administrator of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Yue, also well regarded, served as Attendant-in-Ordinary, chief clerk to Vanguard General Zixu, Prince of Linhai, and Administrator of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 晉安王子勛建偽號，召拜為吏部尚書，與鄧琬共輔偽政。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin'an, Zixun, established a false reign-title, Yue was summoned and appointed Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, assisting the false regime together with Deng Wan.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jin'an Zixun set up a pretender court, Yue was summoned as Minister of Personnel and joined Deng Wan in serving the false government.

sentences.zh: 及事敗，悅殺琬歸降，復為太子中庶子。

translations.literal: When affairs failed, Yue killed Wan and surrendered; he was again made Crown Prince Vice-Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: When the cause collapsed, Yue killed Wan and surrendered; he was again made Crown Prince Vice-Councillor.

sentences.zh: 後拜雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Inspector of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 泰始六年，明帝於巴郡置三巴校尉，以悅補之，加持節、輔師將軍，領巴郡太守。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taishi, Emperor Ming established the Three Ba Commander post in Ba Commandery and appointed Yue to it, with the added credentials of Staff of Authority and Assistant Master General, concurrently serving as Administrator of Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi six Emperor Ming created the Three Ba Commander in Ba Commandery and appointed Yue, with Staff of Authority and the title Assistant Master General, concurrently Administrator of Ba Commandery.

sentences.zh: 未拜，卒。

translations.literal: Before he could assume office, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took up the post, he died.

sentences.zh: 暢子浩，官至義陽王昶征北諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Chang's son Hao rose to Consulting Officer under the General Who Campaigns North for the Prince of Yiyang, Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's son Hao reached the post of consulting officer on the staff of the Prince of Yiyang's northern campaign command.

sentences.zh: 浩弟淹，黃門郎，封廣晉縣子，太子右衛率，東陽太守。

translations.literal: Hao's younger brother Yan was Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, enfeoffed as Viscount of Guangjin County, Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, and Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's brother Yan was Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, Viscount of Guangjin, Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, and Administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 逼郡吏燒臂照佛，百姓有罪，使禮佛贖刑，動至數千拜。

translations.literal: He forced district clerks to burn their arms to illuminate the Buddha; when commoners had offenses, he made them worship the Buddha to redeem punishment — often reaching thousands of prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: He made county clerks burn their arms as lamp-offerings before the Buddha; for commoners' crimes he ordered Buddhist worship in lieu of punishment — often thousands of bows.

sentences.zh: 免官禁錮。

translations.literal: He was dismissed from office and confined.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from office and placed under house arrest.

sentences.zh: 起為光祿勳，與晉安王子勛同逆，軍敗見殺焉。

translations.literal: He was reappointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; he joined the Prince of Jin'an, Zixun, in rebellion and was killed when the army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Restored as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, he rebelled with Prince of Jin'an Zixun and was killed when their army was routed.

sentences.zh: 臣穆等案《高氏小史》，《趙倫之傳》下有《到彥之傳》，而此書獨闕。

translations.literal: The subjects Mu and others note: in Gao's Brief History, beneath the Biography of Zhao Lunzhi there stands the Biography of Dao Yanzhi — yet this book alone lacks it.
translations.idiomatic: Your subjects Mu and others observe that Gao's Brief History places the Biography of Dao Yanzhi after that of Zhao Lunzhi, but this book alone omits it.

sentences.zh: 約之史法，諸帝稱廟號，而謂魏為虜。

translations.literal: In Yue's historiographic method, emperors are called by temple names and Wei is called "barbarian."
translations.idiomatic: By Yue's historiographic rules, emperors are named by temple titles and Wei is called "the barbarians."

sentences.zh: 今帝稱帝號，魏稱魏主，與《南史》體同，而傳末又無史臣論，疑非約書。

translations.literal: Here emperors are called by reign names and Wei is called "Wei ruler," the same form as the Nanshi — yet at the biography's end there is no historians' comment; it is suspected not to be Yue's book.
translations.idiomatic: Here emperors are called by reign titles and Wei by "Wei ruler," as in the Nanshi — yet there is no historians' appraisal at the end; it is doubted to be Yue's original text.

sentences.zh: 然其辭差與《南史》異，故特存焉。

translations.literal: Yet its wording differs somewhat from the Nanshi; therefore it is specially preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Still, its language diverges in places from the Nanshi, and so it is kept here on that account.
